title: INT8 weight-only compatibility matrix, canary orchestration and regression harness
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Integrate INT8 weight-only (GPTQ/AWQ) profiles into our CI/regression pipeline with a reproducible compatibility matrix across model families, sequence lengths, and GPU types. Deliverables: 1) a canonical compatibility matrix and test definitions; 2) a CI job that runs smoke + nightly regression for each profile; 3) a canary rollout orchestration that gates changes based on accuracy and latency deltas; 4) playbook for rollback and for triage of calibration/accuracy regressions. This ticket covers engineering work to wire the harness, add metric collectors, and publish gating thresholds used by release automation.
acceptance_criteria: Compatibility matrix documented in Confluence with entries for small/medium/large model families and both GPTQ and AWQ weight-only variants
CI job 'quant-int8-wo-regress' added to our DAG that executes smoke (fast) and full nightly suites and reports pass/fail to Slack and the console dashboard
Canary rollout flow: new INT8 profile goes to canary (1% traffic) for 24h; automated checks on accuracy delta and latency percentiles must pass before 100% rollout
Automated gating thresholds: absolute generation-quality delta <= 1.0% (or relative <= 3% if baseline small), and 95th latency increase <= 15% for same batch sizes
Regression job produces a report with: golden-prompt corpus results, token-level logit drift histogram, embedding cosine deltas, and per-prompt fail traces linked to PRs
Playbook exists with triage steps, mitigations (recalibrate/roll back to fp16/previous profile/disable quant), and follow-up tickets created for any failing workloads
test_plan: Smoke (10 min): run 5 representative prompts across 3 model sizes on target GPU (A100/H100/T4) comparing baseline FP16 vs INT8-WO (GPTQ/AWQ)
Nightly full: run golden prompt corpus (2k prompts across summarization, instruction, code, Q&A) and compute EM/ROUGE/embedding-cosine distributions
Long-run: 8-hour throughput/latency stability test to catch memory fragmentation or KV cache regressions
Cross-batch: validate batching behavior under concurrency and ensure no off-by-one in KV cache reuse
Canary: incremental traffic rollout with automated snapshotting of sample responses and per-route metrics
compatibility_matrix_summary: Matrix axes: model_family (mistral/llama/reds), size (S/M/L/XL), quantizer (GPTQ, AWQ), GPU (A100, H100, T4), seq_len (128/512/2048), batch_size (1/4/16). Each cell contains: pass/fail, accuracy_delta_pct, 95th_latency_ms_delta, notes on stability and any calibration params used.
calibration_workflow_notes: Calibration runs are separated from regression runs; calibration artifacts stored in gs://redwood-quant-calibrations/<profile>/<model>/<timestamp>. For AWQ we keep per-layer scale tables and a small calibration set fingerprint. Calibration reproducibility is enforced by containerizing the calibration binary and pinning RNG seeds. Calibration failures attach logs + binary checksum to the regression report.
blockers: Need a small GPU quota bump in the shared nightly pool for H100 runs (request submitted to infra). Also waiting on models team to publish AWQ artifact naming convention. If quotas are not available, fallback to synthetic sampling that won't catch memory fragmentation issues.
decisions: Use both GPTQ and AWQ implementations side-by-side in the matrix rather than attempting a convergence layer (keeps triage simpler)
Accept slightly higher latency for INT8 in exchange for ~2.5x throughput increase, but gate based on 95th percentile thresholds
Store calibration artifacts in GCS with a standard path and checksum; calibration is required for any new profile to be eligible for canary
review_feedback: PM review (Jared Kim): ask to tighten acceptance thresholds for customer-critical routes — added a per-route override option
Design/Console (Priya Nair): request to expose 'failed prompts' samples in the console report — added to reporting schema
SRE (Laura Chen): suggested adding a memory-leak long-run; added 8-hour long-run test
